source_quote: Severe acne which may be hard to treat.
note: Listed, but not framed as characteristic, so weak rather than strong. Acne is common enough in the general population that treating it as strong support would raise PCOS on very little.
Skipped periods lengthen the interval between them. Weak because the source names the pattern rather than a day threshold, so the mapping to our over_35_days bucket is ours.

source_quote: Menstrual irregularities: No menstrual periods—called amenorrhea
note: Absent periods are named explicitly, not merely implied by "irregular".
Listed first among the symptoms of PCOS, and corroborated by NICHD, which calls absence of ovulation a characteristic feature.

source_quote: Because the characteristic features of PCOS (also known as Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovary Syndrome [PMOS])—absence of ovulation, indicated by irregular menstrual periods or no periods at all; high androgen levels; and growths in one or both ovaries, often clumps of ovarian follicles that have stopped developing—are wide ranging, so, too, are the symptoms of the condition.
note: THE ELIMINATION ROW. The source frames absence of ovulation as a CHARACTERISTIC feature and states it is indicated by irregular or absent periods, so regular cycles argue against — this is explicit framing, not inference from a symptom list, which the protocol forbids. MedlinePlus corroborates diagnostically: "People with PCOS usually have at least two of these problems: Not ovulating...". Without this row PCOS never drops out of the differential and elimination does not work.

source_quote: Infertility . PCOS is one of the most common causes of infertility. But many women with PCOS can still get pregnant.
note: Weak despite strong language, because the same sentence qualifies it: "many women with PCOS can still get pregnant". The source states a population-level association, not a per-person sign.

source_quote: Too much hair on the face, chest, stomach, or thighs.
note: Named as a main sign on both sources; NICHD calls it hirsutism and ties it to high androgen levels, one of the three characteristic features.

source_quote: Obesity , weight gain, or trouble losing weight.
note: IMPERFECT MAPPING, deliberately weak. The source names obesity, which is a state rather than a change, alongside weight gain, which is a change. Our feature captures change only. Weak support reflects that the row covers part of what the source says, not all of it.

source_quote: Heavy or painful periods or bleeding between periods
note: Same sentence as the row above, which is legitimate — one source sentence supports two cells. Weak rather than strong because bleeding between periods appears last in a list of alternatives rather than being emphasised.

source_quote: Heavy or painful periods or bleeding between periods
note: First symptom listed, and corroborated by NICHD ("Heavy bleeding or painful periods") and by the NHS heavy periods page, which names fibroids among the causes.
